scheme_name: National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI)
overview: National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI) is an umbrella programme conceived and developed by the Technology Translation and Innovation (TTI) Division, Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, for nurturing ideas and innovations (knowledge-based and technology-driven) into successful startups. The programme works in line with national priorities and goals, focusing on building an innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem with the objective of socio-economic development through wealth and job creation. It supports startups through scouting, supporting, and scaling of innovations via components like PRAYAS, EIR, TBI, Accelerator, Seed Support, and Centres of Excellence.
objectives: Nurture ideas and innovations into successful startups
Focus on socio-economic development through wealth and job creation
Support scouting, supporting, and scaling of innovations
Align with national priorities and goals
Promote indigenous innovation and Atmanirbhar Bharat Mission
Strengthen the pipeline of high-quality innovative startups
Establish networks between innovators, academia, mentors, and incubators
eligibility: Eligibility varies by component: For NIDHI-PRAYAS, innovators/startups can apply through NIDHI-PRAYAS Centres at selected TBIs; for NIDHI Seed Support Program, startups must be registered in India, preferably DPIIT-registered, with at least 3 months association with the incubator, clarity on USP, and at least 51% shareholding by Indian promoters; for NIDHI-EIR, applicants must be Indian citizens with minimum 4 years of formal education in science/engineering OR 3 years degree/diploma + 2 years work experience, committed to full-time entrepreneurial pursuit; for NIDHI-TBI, host institutions must be academic/technical/R&D or other entities with clear purpose to promote innovation, in existence for at least 3 years, and not-for-profit legal entities.
benefits: Benefits include financial support (grants up to INR 40 lakhs for prototyping under PRAYAS 2.0, up to INR 100 lakhs under Seed Support, up to INR 30,000/month under EIR), access to infrastructure (Fab Labs, incubation space), mentoring, technical and business guidance, IP and legal assistance, industry and investor connect opportunities, networking events, demo day exposure, and co-working spaces. Non-financial benefits also include training, prototype development support, and ecosystem integration.
financial_support: Financial support varies by component: NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0 offers up to ₹20 lakhs per innovator for PRAYAS Centres and up to ₹40 lakhs for Advance PRAYAS Centres; NIDHI Seed Support Program provides up to INR 1000 lakh to incubators (released in phases) and up to INR 100 lakh per startup; NIDHI-EIR offers a monthly stipend of INR 10,000–30,000 for up to 18 months; NIDHI-Accelerator provides up to INR 40 lakh per cohort (INR 30 lakh for program, INR 10 lakh for demo day awards); NIDHI-CoE offers enhanced support of INR 50 crore over 5 years for selected incubators.
application_process: Application process varies by component: For NIDHI-PRAYAS 2.0, innovators apply to designated PRAYAS Centres/Advance PRAYAS Centres via the NIDHI PRAYAS Portal using a common application template; for NIDHI Seed Support Program, incubators apply once per year through an online portal (call announced annually), and startups apply to listed incubators/TBIs; for NIDHI-EIR, startups apply through NIDHI-EIR Centres at selected TBIs; for NIDHI-TBI, proposals are submitted to NSTEDB via their online portal with required enclosures; for NIDHI-Accelerator, TBIs apply through the department’s online portal http://onlinedst.gov.in.

deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round for most components; however, specific calls like NIDHI Seed Support Program are announced once per year, and Indo-German InnoXchange Programme had a deadline of 10th April, 2026.
implementing_agency: Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, through the National Science & Technology Entrepreneurship Development Board (NSTEDB) and Technology Translation and Innovation (TTI) Division
